Statement This Important flaw in the axios JavaScript library allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service. By submitting crafted form data with excessively nested bracket-delimited field names, an attacker can trigger uncontrolled recursion in the formDataToJSON function (exposed as axios.formToJSON() and used internally by the default transformRequest when FormData is sent with Content-Type: application/json), exhausting the JavaScript call stack and causing a RangeError that may terminate the application process. This vulnerability affects applications that pass attacker-controlled FormData field names to axios' FormData-to-JSON conversion. Mitigation Upgrade to axios >= 1.18.0 (1.x) or >= 0.33.0 (0.x), which add recursion depth guards to formDataToJSON. If an immediate upgrade is not possible, validate and limit the nesting depth of FormData field names before passing them to axios.formToJSON() or before sending FormData through axios with Content-Type: application/json, and ensure error handling is in place to catch RangeError exceptions from this code path. The record gives CVSS 7.5 (High) with availability impact. The axios advisory rates it Moderate, 6.3. The weakness is CWE-400, uncontrolled resource consumption. A closely related entry, CVE-2026-67313, describes the same recursion in the same helper. Its advisory lists only 1.18.0 as the patched version. Upgrade to the versions named here and you cover both. The advisory is specific about the conditions. Applications are affected only when untrusted users can control FormData key names that axios converts, either through a direct call to axios.formToJSON() or when FormData is sent with a JSON content type. Plain multipart uploads, and the toFormData helper that already limits depth, are not affected. How to check if you're exposed Find every copy of axios, direct and transitive: npm ls axios npm why axios Yarn and pnpm users can run yarn why axios or pnpm why axios. Look at the lockfile too, since a transitive dependency can pin an older copy than your top level package.json suggests. Then search your code for formToJSON and for places where FormData is sent with a JSON content type. If neither appears, the vulnerable function is not called, though the version is still old. The advisory says that the failure is a RangeError for maximum call stack size exceeded. In its testing it can be caught, so whether a process dies depends on how your code handles the error. What to do now Upgrade axios to 1.18.0, or 0.33.0 on the 0.x line, in every project and lockfile. Search for formToJSON and JSON serialization of FormData in your code. Limit the depth and length of field names you accept from users, at the edge. Handle rejected promises and thrown errors around these calls so one request cannot take down a worker. Paste your dependency file into the free in-browser scan at gold.safeguard.sh/scan to see which of your projects pull in an affected version.
